newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says no talks over Garuda stake.
newsitem.headline: KLM says no talks over Garuda stake.

text.p: Dutch flag carrier KLM said on Tuesday it was not holding talks with state-owned Indonesian Garuda with a view to taking a stake in the company.
Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf reported earlier on Tuesday that KLM was considering taking a 25 percent stake in Garuda, which is scheduled for privatisation in 1998.

"Garuda is one of KLM's partners but there have been no discussions over taking a stake. Representatives from the two companies often meet but a stake is not an issue at the moment," KLM spokeswoman Marjolein Wenting told Reuters.
De Telegraaf, quoting Garuda officials in Jakarta, said Indonesia's transport minister had held talks with KLM chairman Pieter Bouw over extending the co-operation pact between the two airlines.
"Garuda is a KLM partner and KLM's name often comes up in stories about Garuda's privatisation," Wenting added.
